title: Knotline — GPU runway docket
body:
Quick morning scratchpad for the midweek runway. Unpolished — doing this live while triaging.

Context / goals:
- Get the holiday-batch GPU pools back to steady-state (target: < 10% spare overcommit).
- Finish the small QoS change to preemptible routing so low-priority jobs don't steal H100s.
- Validate rack 12B thermal sensors after the swap last night.

Top-of-mind checklist (ordered):
1) Pool utilization audit (08:30)
   - command: gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels:gpu-pool:holiday-batch" -> capture node list
   - quick metrics: target throughput 2.2k tok/s per A100; live: ? (check prometheus graph -> link in slack)
   - notes: saw two nodes in 12B with large free mem but pod placement failing. Possibly runc / docker bug.

2) Node drain + reprovision plan
   - suspect nodes: node-12b-07, node-12b-08
   - drain command (one-by-one): kubectl drain node-12b-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
   - after drain: reboot, check kernel dmesg for ECC warnings, rejoin.
   - TODO: add ephemeral label before drain: kubectl label node node-12b-07 transient-maint=2025-02-12

3) H100 vs A100 placement policy (short term)
   - immediate: enforce scheduling affinity so canary jobs prefer A100 for now (we're low on H100).
   - create k8s taint/ toleration? plan: taint h100 nodes as 'h100-only:NoSchedule' and update lower-priority workloads to have toleration temporarily.
   - question: who owns the scheduler policy change? ping @leah in Slack (done).

4) Network flakiness observed at 07:40
   - symptom: intermittent 5–20ms packet loss to rack 9 (affects grpc idle pings).
   - quick check: run iperf between node-9a-03 and node-9a-10; check switch counters on leaf-9a.
   - escalation path: if switch counters show CRCs -> open NOC ticket, reference JIRA-OPS-1842.

5) Capacity planning quick math (for noon deploy)
   - expected spike: +35% token throughput from hosted-api experiment (12:00 - 14:00).
   - buffer: add 6 A100 nodes to ‘burst’ pool (temp), configure autoscaler to prefer burst pool before spinning up dedicated nodes.
   - action: submit AC request to clouds team with estimate (Rough numbers pasted below).

Mini numbers (scratch):
Node  | GPU  | Free mem | Est tok/s
node-10a-02 | A100 40GB | 12GB | 1800
node-11b-05 | H100 80GB | 22GB | 4200
node-12b-07 | A100 80GB | 6GB  | 1500 (degraded)

Reminders / short TODOs:
- [ ] Upload kernel logs from node-12b-07 to ticket (s3://infra-logs/ravi/12b-07-2025-02-11.tar.gz)
- [ ] Add autoscaler policy comment to PR (#298) — note: set cooldown to 4m
- [ ] Run the small quant test for model 'vicuna-13b-q4' on a reclaimed A100 to validate perf drop 
- [ ] Update ops-runbook note about preferring kv-cache warmup on cold starts (tiny blurb)

Snippets & commands to copy quickly:
- kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running -l app=worker,env=holiday-batch
- kubectl drain node-12b-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- ssh root@node-12b-07 'journalctl -b -1 | tail -n 200' > /tmp/12b07-logs.txt
- iperf3 -c 10.0.9.10 -t 60 -P 6

Odd behaviours / notes to chase later:
- Some long-tail latencies in small token workloads when KV cache miss coincides with network hiccup. Hypothesis: small RPCs amplified by kernel NIC interrupt steering weirdness after kernel update.
- Need to track when kernel 6.6.4 rolled to racks 9/12 — who merged the kernel bump earlier this month? link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/277 (maybe related).

Questions for morning sync (ping list):
- @Carlos: can you confirm if node-12b-08 had a forced reboot by KMS yesterday?
- @Leah: do we want to toggle the H100 taint today or wait for the afternoon deploy?
- @SRE-oncall: if network CRCs show up we escalate or reroute? quick agreed process?

End-of-shift handoff notes (fill before leaving):
- state of drained nodes: (write names)
- outstanding tickets opened: (JIRA ids)
- who to wake if things go sideways: pager list included in team runbook

Notes-to-self (messy):
- If repeated slow token rates persist after drain, try limiting active concurrent sessions per node to 8 and measure.
- Save a copy of the A100 perf profile before applying the quant patch.
- Remember: this is a warm-start experiment; don't flip autoscaler policies globally.

Scratch links (for copy/paste during triage):
- Prometheus: https://prom.redwood-infra/internal/graph?g0.expr=avg%20by(node)(irate(gpu_token_throughput[5m]))
- SRE runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/infra-shift-handbook
- PR to watch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/298

That's it — stop overthinking, run the planned drains one at a time, and keep the canary live until midday.

— R"
